name: Capucine Buff
lede: Capucine Buff is a pale peach-buff named for capucine, the French word for nasturtium and for a Capuchin friar's robe, recorded by Ridgway in 1912.

sections.title: Nasturtium or friar's robe
sections.body:
Our library dates Capucine Buff to Ridgway's 1912 standards, plate III, hue 13, with Maerz and Paul's 1930 dictionary adding its own first record in 1912 at plate 9, swatch E5 [1]. *Capucine* is French for the nasturtium flower and, before that, for the hooded robe of a Capuchin friar; dictionaries use both senses for the family of orange-buff names, and our data does not settle which one this particular swatch follows [1].

It builds on [[buff]][1]. Our library's nearest everyday match is Peach, 4.2 units of ΔE away, with Warm Buff and Light Ochraceous-Buff listed as closer Ridgway near-duplicates [1].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive finds a close match to Capucine Buff in 283 of 23,781 paintings (1.19 percent), as photographed [2]. Henri Matisse used it most relative to his own museums' baseline, in 4 of his 50 works here, 4.7 times expected [2]. It most often plays a light tone inside a painting, and keeps company with Camel more than chance [2]. These are screen approximations of aged paintings, not pigment readings [2].
